Network restructuring

The branch that looked worst on cost was not the structural problem

How diagnostic evidence changed a proposed three-branch consolidation and preserved two viable sites.

3branches reviewed
1structurally unviable
2retained in the network
16branches in the wider routing model

The situation

Three branches were below target on cost per order, capacity utilisation and customer satisfaction. The initial proposal was to close two and merge the third.

The score was real. The question was whether it was locating the cause.

Three different causes

One branch had contracted demand and unworkable fixed lease economics. A second was receiving centrally routed orders outside its natural catchment. A third had been without a permanent manager for eleven months.

The rebuild

One branch closed, the routing model was corrected across the 16-branch network and a permanent manager was installed at the third site with a six-month recovery plan.

Measured result

Two of the three branches proposed for closure remained in the network. The cost and capacity targets that triggered the review were met without the original consolidation.

Historical operator track record. Company name withheld. Metrics and factual framing follow the confirmed September 2026 case-study source.
